method.label: Choose digit subsets and remove overlap

annotationRationale: Sorting digit subsets gives bijections with the two families of numbers. The multiplication principle counts subsets, and two-set inclusion-exclusion removes the nine duplicated one-digit numbers.
sourceMethod: Followed the official subset-bijection method and subtraction of the one-digit overlap, making the zero restrictions and uniqueness explicit.

review.mathCheck: Increasing numbers correspond to 511 nonempty subsets of digits 1–9. Decreasing numbers correspond to 1022 subsets of digits 0–9 after excluding the empty subset and {0}. Exactly nine positive one-digit numbers overlap, giving 511+1022−9=1524, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution #11's two subset bijections and inclusion-exclusion. The candidate explicitly justifies leading-zero exclusions, uniqueness, and the overlap.
review.annotationCheck: The selected nodes cover the encodings, binary subset choices, and union count without material omissions.
